summary_for_children: At-Tahrim tells believers to protect their families with good deeds and gives two examples of faith: the wife of Pharaoh and Maryam.
environment_concept: A palace room (66:11) and a quiet sanctuary with fruit in a lit niche (66:12). No one is shown.
architecture_and_scenery: A palace interior and a modest sanctuary.

areas.name: Palace Room
areas.description: A room in Pharaoh's palace; no one shown.

activities.name: Sincere repentance
activities.description: Plant three beds as a fresh start; they bloom.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A village garden in the morning with flower beds, a water jar, a gate and a fence, and a trail of muddy footprints

primary_mechanic.text: Follow your own muddy footprints back through the garden and put right each thing you spoiled on the way: a trampled flower bed, a knocked-over jar, a gate left open, a broken fence rail (66:8, turning back sincerely; making amends as one part of it).

secondary_activities: being close is not enough (66:10, read)
unique_world.narrative_structure: The footprint trail with four things to put right, then two plaques of examples
world_assets: flower bed, jar, gate and fence that change when fixed
environment_behaviour: each spoiled thing returns to how it should be
the footprints fade once all is put right
unique_world.learning_objective: Understand turning back to Allah sincerely and putting right what we spoiled (66:8)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: Learning from Our Choices
story_library.children_narration: Surah At-Tahrim includes lessons about responsibility within households and examples of women who made different choices. It reminds us that every person is responsible for their own faith and actions. Maryam is presented as an example of devotion.

world_idea.title: The Gallery of Examples
world_idea.description: Discover narrated lessons through separate historical-style environments and reflect on sincerity and personal responsibility.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The four women (66:10-12) are not shown; they appear only as readings.
